# ankra_application_environment (Resource)

Settings of one environment of an application (`ankra application environments set`): its name, its own "who runs it" layer, which applies over the application's, and its operating expectations. Environments come from where the application is deployed, so this resource adopts an existing one and never creates or deletes it. The layer is managed only when `level`, `areas` or `limits` is set, and is replaced as a whole, starting from the stored layer so a change made meanwhile is refused. Operating expectations are adopted as a new revision over the current one. Each part is written only when it changes. A caller confined to a project manages only environments placed in it. Cloning an environment onto another cluster stays imperative. Destroy leaves the environment's settings as they are.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ankra_application_environment" "production" {
  application_id = ankra_application.web.id
  environment_id = "8f1d2c3b-4a5e-4f60-9b7a-1c2d3e4f5a6b"
  name           = "production"
  level          = "you_run_it"

  operating_expectations = {
    availability_percent = 99.9
    data_region          = "eu"
    recovery_minutes     = 60
    data_loss_minutes    = 15
    retention_days       = 30
    monthly_budget_cents = 50000
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `application_id` (String) Identifier of the application. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `environment_id` (String) Identifier of one of the application's environments. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `areas` (Map of String) Per-area levels, keyed by area: `keep_it_up`, `ship_changes`, `keep_it_safe`, `keep_costs_down`, `keep_it_current` or `fix_my_code`.
- `level` (String) Who runs every area of the environment unless `areas` says otherwise: `you_run_it`, `together` or `ankra_runs_it`. Unset leaves it to the layer below.
- `limits` (Attributes) Limits on what Ankra may do unasked. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--limits))
- `name` (String) Name of the environment. Setting it renames the environment; one still named after its cluster cannot be renamed yet.
- `operating_expectations` (Attributes) The environment's operating expectations: intent Ankra plans and reports against. They do not provision or certify runtime controls. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--operating_expectations))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<application_id>/<environment_id>`.
- `operating_expectations_revision` (Number) Revision of the adopted operating expectations; null when none was adopted.
- `role` (String) Role of the environment: `playground`, `production`, `staging`, `development` or `custom`.

<a id="nestedatt--limits"></a>
### Nested Schema for `limits`

Optional:

- `may_change_data` (Boolean) Whether a change may alter data.
- `monthly_cost_increase_cents` (Number) Most a change may add to the monthly cost, in cents.
- `non_production_downtime_seconds` (Number) Most downtime a change may cause outside production, in seconds.
- `production_downtime_seconds` (Number) Most downtime a change may cause in production, in seconds.


<a id="nestedatt--operating_expectations"></a>
### Nested Schema for `operating_expectations`

Required:

- `availability_percent` (Number) Availability aimed for, 90 to 100 percent.
- `data_loss_minutes` (Number) Most data loss acceptable, 0 to 10080 minutes.
- `data_region` (String) Where data may live: `eu`, `us` or `any`.
- `monthly_budget_cents` (Number) Monthly budget, in cents.
- `recovery_minutes` (Number) Longest acceptable recovery, 1 to 10080 minutes.
- `retention_days` (Number) How long backups are kept, 1 to 3650 days.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Imported by <application_id>/<environment_id>.
terraform import ankra_application_environment.production 5b0c4a9e-2f43-4b8e-9a51-1f0d8e7c2a10/8f1d2c3b-4a5e-4f60-9b7a-1c2d3e4f5a6b
```
